regions.translation: [effe]ctual in fevers and hot distempers of the body, head, eyes, and other parts, and for all the purposes aforesaid. The leaves boiled in lye, and the head washed with it, heal the itch and its running sores, and make the hair black. The powder of the leaves strewed on cankerous and running ulcers wonderfully helps to heal them. Some condense the juice of the leaves, and some the juice of the berries, to keep for their use all the year, for the purposes aforesaid.

regions.text:
It is a Plant of Venus in Aries : You ſhall
have ſom Directions at the latter end of the
Book for the gathering of al Herbs and Plants
&c. If any ask the Reaſon why Venus is ſo
prickly ? Tel them 'tis becauſe ſhe is in the
houſe of Mars.
regions.translation: It is a plant of Venus in Aries. You shall have some directions at the latter end of the book for the gathering of all herbs and plants, etc. If any ask the reason why Venus is so prickly, tell them it is because she is in the house of Mars.

regions.text: Blites.
regions.translation: Blites [blite; Amaranthus blitum].

regions.text: Deſcription.
regions.translation: Description.

regions.text:
OF theſe there are two ſorts commonly
known, Viz. White and Red. The
White hath Leavs ſomwhat like unto Beets,
but ſmaller, rounder and of a whitiſh green co-
lour, every one ſtanding upon a ſmal long
Footſtalk : The Stalk riſeth up two or three
foot high with ſuch like Leavs theron: The
Flowers grow at the top in long round tufts or
cluſters,wherein are contained ſmal and round
Seed. The Root is very full of threeds or
ſtrings.
regions.translation: Of these there are two sorts commonly known, namely white and red. The white has leaves somewhat like beets, but smaller, rounder, and of a whitish green colour, every one standing on a small long footstalk. The stalk rises up two or three feet high with similar leaves on it. The flowers grow at the top in long round tufts or clusters, in which are contained small round seeds. The root is very full of threads or strings.

regions.text:
The red Blite is in all things like the white,
but that his Leavs and tufted heads are excee-
ding red at firſt,and after turn more Purpliſh.
regions.translation: The red blite is in all things like the white, except that its leaves and tufted heads are exceedingly red at first, and afterwards turn more purplish.

regions.text:
There are other kinds of Blites which grow
wild, differing from the two former ſorts but
little, only the wild are ſmaler in every part.
regions.translation: There are other kinds of blites which grow wild, differing but little from the two former sorts, only the wild ones are smaller in every part.

regions.text: Place.
regions.translation: Place.

regions.text:
They grow in Gardens, and wild in many
places of this Land.
regions.translation: They grow in gardens, and wild in many places of this land.

regions.text: Time.
regions.translation: Time.

regions.text: They ſeed in Auguſt and September.
regions.translation: They seed in August and September.

regions.text: Vertues and uſe.
regions.translation: Virtues and use.

regions.text:
They are all of them cooling, drying and
binding, ſerving to reſtrain the Fluxes of
Bloud in either man or woman, eſpecially the
Red ; which alſo ſtayeth the overflowing of
women's Reds, as the white Blite ſtayeth the
Whites in Women. It is an excellent ſecret,
you cannot wel fail in the uſe ; they are al un-
der the Dominion of Venus.
regions.translation: They are all of them cooling, drying, and binding, serving to restrain fluxes of blood in either man or woman, especially the red, which also stays the overflowing of women's reds [excessive menstrual bleeding], as the white blite stays the whites [leucorrhoea] in women. It is an excellent secret; you cannot well fail in the use. They are all under the dominion of Venus.

regions.text:
Reds and
Whites in
Women.
regions.translation:
Reds and
whites in
women [menstrual flux and leucorrhoea].

regions.text:
There is one other ſort of wild Blites, like
the other wild kinds,but having long and ſpike
heads of greeniſh Seed, ſeeming by the thick
ſetting together to be al Seed.
regions.translation: There is one other sort of wild blites, like the other wild kinds, but having long spiked heads of greenish seed, seeming by their thick setting together to be all seed.

regions.text:
This ſort the Fiſhes are delighted with, and
it is a good and uſual Bait ; for Fiſhes will
bite faſt enough at them, if you have but wit
enough to catch them when they bite.
regions.translation: This sort the fishes are delighted with, and it is a good and usual bait; for fishes will bite fast enough at them, if you have but wit enough to catch them when they bite.

regions.text: Time.
regions.translation: Time.

regions.text:
They flower in June and July, and the
Seed is ripe ſhortly after.
regions.translation: They flower in June and July, and the seed is ripe shortly after.

regions.text: Vertues and uſe.
regions.translation: Virtues and use.

regions.text:
They are very Cordial. The Leaves or
Roots are to very good purpoſe uſed in putrid
and Peſtilential Feavers, to defend the Heart,
and hlp to reſiſt and expel the Poyſon, or the
Venom of other Creatures ; the Seed is of the
like effect ; and the Seed and Leavs are good
to encreaſe Milk in Womens Breaſts : The
Leavs, Flowers and Seed, all, or any of them
are good to expel Penſiveneſs and Melanchol-
y : it helpeth to clarifie the Bloud, and miti-
gate heat in Feavers. The Juyce made into a
Syrup prevaileth much to all the purpoſes a-
foreſaid, and is put with other cooling, open-
ing, clenſing Herbs,to open obſtructions, and
help the yellow-Jaundice, and mixed with Fu-
mitory, to cool, clenſ, and temper the Blood,
therby it helpeth the Itch, Ringworms, and
Tetters, or other ſpreading Scabs or Sores.
The Flowers candied, or made into a Con-
ſerve are helping in the former cauſes, but are
chiefly uſed as a Cordial,and is good for thoſe
that are weak with long ſickneſs, and to com-
fort the Heart and Spirits of thoſe that are in a
conſumption,or troubled wth often ſwoonings,
or paſſions of the Heart : The Diſtilled Wa-
ter is no leſs effectual to all the purpoſes afore-
ſaid, and helpeth the redneſs and inflamati-
on of the Eyes being waſhed therewith : The
dried Herb is never uſed, but the green ; yet
the Aſhes therof boyled in Mead, or Honyed
Water is available againſt Inflamations and
Ulcers in the Mouth or Throat, to waſh and
gargle it therewith. The Roots of Bugloſs are
effectual being made into a licking Electuarie,
for the Cough, and to condenſate thin flegm,
and Rhewmatick Diſtillations upon the
Lungs.
regions.translation: They are very cordial. The leaves or roots are used to very good purpose in putrid and pestilential fevers, to defend the heart, and to help resist and expel the poison, or the venom of other creatures; the seed is of the like effect; and the seed and leaves are good to increase milk in women's breasts. The leaves, flowers, and seed, all or any of them, are good to expel pensiveness and melancholy. It helps to clarify the blood and mitigate heat in fevers. The juice made into a syrup avails much for all the purposes aforesaid, and is put with other cooling, opening, cleansing herbs to open obstructions and help the yellow jaundice, and, mixed with fumitory, to cool, cleanse, and temper the blood, whereby it helps the itch, ringworms, and tetters, or other spreading scabs or sores. The flowers, candied or made into a conserve, are helpful in the former cases, but are chiefly used as a cordial, and are good for those that are weak with long sickness, and to comfort the heart and spirits of those that are in a consumption, or troubled with frequent swoonings or passions of the heart. The distilled water is no less effectual for all the purposes aforesaid, and helps the redness and inflammation of the eyes when they are washed with it. The dried herb is never used, but only the green; yet the ashes of it, boiled in mead or honeyed water, are of use against inflammations and ulcers in the mouth or throat, to wash and gargle it with. The roots of bugloss are effectual when made into a licking electuary, for the cough, and to condense thin phlegm and rheumatic distillations upon the lungs.

regions.text:
They are both Herbs of Jupiter, and under
Leo, both great Cordials, great ſtrengthners
of Nature.
regions.translation: They are both herbs of Jupiter, and under Leo; both great cordials, great strengtheners of nature.
